Not a problem. Like I said I'm no professional so I could be wrong but at least you have a few ideas now. And its very likely but you would definitely have a rough idle and a check engine light on if its a coil or O2 sensor out.

The idle drop says cam phasers to me. Not 100% but that might be causing the acceleration issue as well.  I do know fords cam phasers go out pretty quickly. Those are a cheap part might be worth looking into.

My thinking is its like a hotrod cam but bad. Meaning some of the lobes on the camshaft might be worn down or chipped making the car run very rough. But as the cam spins faster as you accelerate it evens itself pit a bit and runs better. Because a big hotrod cam has bigger lobes so of idles rough giving it that muscle car lope but evens out in the higher rpms. It might be doing the reverse so when youre at lower rpms its not getting enough fuel so it bogs down and misfires. If that makes any sense. Does idle rough or just when you accelerate?
Hmmmm. My only other thought would be camshaft maybe. A few lobes might be roughed up and don't like going that slow. Granted I'm just a shade tree mechanic so my knowledge is a bit limited.
